title: Kirby Problem 1.12
exact_target: For a knot in an oriented three-manifold, Dehn filling along a slope on its peripheral torus produces a closed three-manifold. Two fillings are purely cosmetic if their resulting manifolds are orientation-preservingly homeomorphic; they are chirally cosmetic if an orientation-reversing homeomorphism identifies the results. The question has four parts. Can inequivalent slopes ever be purely cosmetic? If two knots in a closed oriented three-manifold have orientation-preservingly homeomorphic complements, must an ambient homeomorphism carry one knot to the other? Does every nontrivial knot in $S^3$ admit no purely cosmetic pair? Finally, must a knot in $S^3$ other than a torus knot $T_{2g+1,2}$ admit no chirally cosmetic pair of inequivalent slopes?
